# wso2is_external_claim (Resource)

Maps a claim of an external dialect to a local claim. You can also use the built-in dialects:

* `http://wso2.org/oidc/claim` holds the OIDC claims. Add them to tokens with `wso2is_oidc_scope`.
* `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User`, `urn:scim:wso2:schema` and `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User` hold SCIM attributes.

A new server has no custom SCIM dialect. The provider creates it when you add the first claim to it, and leaves it in place when you destroy the resource. To import, use the ID `<dialect_uri>|<claim_uri>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wso2is_external_claim" "department" {
  dialect_uri            = "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim"
  claim_uri              = "department"
  mapped_local_claim_uri = "http://wso2.org/claims/department"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `claim_uri` (String) External claim URI, for example `employee_id` (OIDC) or `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User:employeeId` (SCIM). Changing it replaces the claim.
- `dialect_uri` (String) Dialect URI. Changing it replaces the claim.
- `mapped_local_claim_uri` (String) Local claim URI it maps to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<dialect id>/<claim id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_external_claim.department "http://wso2.org/oidc/claim|department"
```
